title: Data Loss Prevention in Microsoft 365: Policies That Actually Work
description:
A new DLP policy blocks everything on Monday, and by Friday half the finance team is mailing files from personal accounts. This episode is for Microsoft 365 admins and compliance owners who want Purview DLP policies people actually accept. You'll learn how to detect the right data, guide users with tips and overrides, test safely, triage alerts and measure what really works.
In this episode
00:00 – Why block-first DLP fails06:46 – The new model: context, not content alone12:37 – Detection: SITs, EDM, classifiers and labels25:29 – Policy tips and user overrides31:27 – Simulation, tuning, scoping and exceptions47:26 – Endpoint DLP, Teams, Copilot and cloud apps57:10 – Alert triage and measuring effectiveness73:48 – Phased rollout and common failure patterns
Key takeaways
DLP policies built to block drive users to invisible workarounds, so design policies that use context and guide people with tips before enforcing.Run every policy in simulation for weeks, then with tips but no enforcement, and block only high-confidence, high-volume risks with a reporting path.Treat DLP as an ongoing practice with a named owner, weekly tuning from overrides and triage, owned and expiring exceptions, and metrics like true positive rate instead of block counts.
Worth quoting
“it's failing for one reason. Not the tools, the model behind it. Policies built to block lose to policies built to guide.” – Mirko Peters (00:22)
“A credit card number in an email to a payment processor is business. The same number in an email to a personal address is a problem.” – Mirko Peters (02:17)
